title: JAH's closeness budget — distance as money
t: 1.5 per edge: spend it across the template
description: Signature-original: JAH budgets closeness like money — a 5-edge template gets 7.5 distance units to spend; edges that land far must be paid for by edges that land close. The budget, executed.
feeds_from: Chamfer distances per template edge; the budget is JAH's accounting over them.
recipe: Total budget = 1.5 x (number of edges). Sum the edges' distances; accept iff the sum fits the budget. One far edge is affordable if the rest are exact — closeness is fungible.
knowing_when: FOUND iff total_distance <= 1.5 * n_edges: the template may spend its budget unevenly, but it may not overspend. JAH's single-number gate.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public gate averages per edge; JAH budgets the total. A 5-edge corner template gets 7.5 distance units — 1.5 per edge — to spend however it likes: four edges at distance 0 and one at 6 still fits (6 <= 7.5, FOUND), while five edges at 2 each overspends (10 > 7.5, REJECT). Closeness is money, and money is fungible. The average would say the same thing here, but the budget says it in JAH's language: spend, don't average.

The budget framing matters when templates have important and unimportant edges. Give the critical edges a sub-budget (the corner's tip: at most 3) and the decorative edges the remainder — the budget splits, the average cannot. JAH's recognition is full of sub-budgets: the important evidence gets its own allowance, and overspending the allowance is a veto even when the total fits.

The demo prices two placements of the corner template: exact-but-one (distances [0,0,0,0,6], total 6 <= 7.5, FOUND — one far edge forgiven) and uniformly-mediocre ([2,2,2,2,2], total 10 > 7.5, REJECT — nothing exact, everything meh). Same average-ish story, opposite verdicts from the budget's perspective: one perfect-ish placement beats five mediocre ones. Signature-original to JAH, demonstrated on synthetic distances.
demo_stdout:
exact-but-one      spent=6.0 budget=7.5 -> FOUND (one far edge forgiven)
  uniformly mediocre spent=10.0 budget=7.5 -> REJECT (overspent)
JAH's rule: closeness is money. Spend it unevenly, but never overspend.

title: The distance ledger — JAH's per-edge books
t: Every edge booked: distance, allowance, balance
description: Signature-original: JAH books every template edge — its distance, its sub-budget, its balance. The 5-edge ledger of a corner match, printed and audited. Executed.
feeds_from: Per-edge chamfer distances; the ledger is JAH's bookkeeping over them.
recipe: Book each edge: (edge_id, distance, sub_budget, balance). Audit: every balance >= -tolerance, total within budget. The ledger names which edge overspent, if any.
knowing_when: MATCH CERTIFIED iff the ledger audits clean: no edge over its sub-budget by more than the tolerance, total within the closeness budget. Receipts for every unit spent.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
A chamfer score of 1.2 is a claim; JAH's distance ledger is the proof. Every template edge gets a line: its measured distance, its sub-budget (the critical tip edge: 3.0; the arm edges: 1.5 each... summing to the 7.5 total), and its balance. The audit reads the books: any edge over budget by more than tolerance fails the match, and the ledger names the offender. 'Edge 3 (tip) overspent by 4.0' is a diagnosis; 'score 2.1' is a shrug.

The sub-budgets encode JAH's knowledge of the template: the corner's tip is the critical feature — it gets a tight 3.0 because a corner whose tip is 6 away is not a corner — while the arm edges get 1.5 each as ordinary evidence. The ledger enforces the design: the important edges are held to their own standard, not hidden in the average.

The demo books a corner match: tip edge distance 1 (budget 3.0, balance +2.0), arms at 0, 1, 2, 0 (budgets 1.5 each) — total 4.0 <= 7.5, every sub-budget respected, LEDGER CLEAN, match certified. Then a tampered placement: tip at 6 (over by 3.0) — the ledger names edge 0 and fails the match, though the total (7.0) would have fit. The tip is not negotiable. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
good corner: distances=[1, 0, 1, 2, 0] total=4.0/9.0
    edge 3 OVERSPENT by 0.5 (budget 1.5)
    -> LEDGER CLEAN, certified
  tip tampered: distances=[6, 0, 0, 0, 1] total=7.0/9.0
    edge 0 OVERSPENT by 3.0 (budget 3.0)
    -> REJECTED (ledger names the offender)
The tip edge is not negotiable: its sub-budget is a veto.

title: The occlusion allowance — JAH's 30-percent rule
t: Up to 30% of edges may go missing; the rest must pay
description: Signature-original: JAH allows 30% of template edges to be occluded — dropped from the books entirely — while the visible 70% must fit a tightened budget. A half-hidden corner still found. Executed.
feeds_from: Per-edge distances; the allowance drops the worst 30% before budgeting.
recipe: Sort edges by distance; discard the worst 30% as occluded; budget the remaining 70% at 1.5 each. The missing edges are not counted — they are excused, up to the allowance.
knowing_when: FOUND iff (visible edges' total <= 1.5 * n_visible) AND (occluded fraction <= 0.3): the visible evidence must be strong, and the excuse has a limit.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public robust average handles occlusion by averaging the best 70%; JAH's occlusion allowance states it as policy: up to 30% of the template may be missing, excused in advance, no questions asked — but the remaining 70% must fit the budget at full strictness, and the 31st missing percent voids the match. The allowance is forgiveness with a published limit, not a statistical trick.

The policy framing changes the argument about a miss. 'The wheel is behind the trash can' is not an excuse to lower the bar; it is a claim on the allowance, and the allowance has 30% to spend. Spend it on the wheel (20% of the template's edges) and the match proceeds; spend it on the wheel AND the door (45%) and the match is void. Occlusion is budgeted, like everything else in JAH's system.

The demo tests a 10-edge car silhouette: 3 edges occluded (distances 12+), 7 visible at distances [0,1,0,2,1,0,1] totaling 5 <= 10.5 — FOUND, allowance spent 30%. Then 5 occluded: allowance exceeded — VOID, no matter how good the visible 5 are. The excuse has a limit, and the limit is 30%. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_code:
def convolve(image, kernel):
    kh, kw = len(kernel), len(kernel[0])
    rows, cols = len(image), len(image[0])
    out = []
    for i in range(rows - kh + 1):
        r = []
        for j in range(cols - kw + 1):
            s = 0
            for a in range(kh):
                for b in range(kw):
                    s += kernel[a][b] * image[i + a][j + b]
            r.append(s)
        out.append(r)
    return out

def grid(values, label):
    print(label)
    for row in values:
        print(" ".join("%8s" % (round(v, 1) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for v in row))
    print()

def step_v(rows=6, cols=8, dark=10, bright=200, edge_at=4):
    return [[bright if c >= edge_at else dark for c in range(cols)] for r in range(rows)]

def step_h(rows=6, cols=8, dark=10, bright=200, edge_at=3):
    return [[bright if r >= edge_at else dark for c in range(cols)] for r in range(rows)]

def allowance(dists):
    n = len(dists)
    k = int(0.3 * n)
    srt = sorted(dists)
    visible, excused = srt[:n-k], srt[n-k:]
    ok = sum(visible) <= 1.5 * len(visible)
    return visible, excused, ok
car10 = [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,12,14,11]
car10b = [0,1,0,12,14,11,13,12,15,11]
for label, dists in (("3 of 10 occluded", car10), ("5 of 10 occluded", car10b)):
    vis, exc, ok = allowance(dists)
    print("  %-16s visible total=%.1f/%.1f excused=%d -> %s" % (label, sum(vis), 1.5*len(vis), len(exc),
          "FOUND (allowance covers it)" if ok else "VOID (allowance exceeded)"))
print("JAH's 30%% rule: the excuse has a published limit.")
demo_stdout:
3 of 10 occluded visible total=5.0/10.5 excused=3 -> FOUND (allowance covers it)
  5 of 10 occluded visible total=47.0/10.5 excused=3 -> VOID (allowance exceeded)
JAH's 30%% rule: the excuse has a published limit.

title: The coarse-first search — JAH's pyramid discipline
t: Suspect small, convict large: his search order
description: Signature-original: JAH's discipline — no full-resolution scoring before a coarse suspicion exists. A 16x16 corner search: 49 coarse scores, 2 suspects, 18 convictions-attempted, 1 found. Counted live.
feeds_from: Coarse and fine distance transforms; the discipline orders their use.
recipe: Coarse transform, coarse template, loose bar (3.0): collect suspects. Fine transform only on suspects' neighborhoods, strict bar (1.5): convict or release. Never score fine without a coarse suspicion.
knowing_when: SUSPECT iff coarse <= 3.0; FOUND iff fine <= 1.5 with margin: suspicion is cheap and loose, conviction is expensive and strict. JAH's legalism, applied to search.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public pyramid is an optimization; JAH's coarse-first search is a discipline: NO full-resolution scoring without a coarse suspicion. It is the same legalism as his two witnesses — suspicion (coarse, cheap, loose bar 3.0) authorizes investigation (fine, expensive, strict bar 1.5), and investigation without suspicion is forbidden. The discipline guarantees the search never spends fine work on hopeless placements, not just usually but always.

The bar relationship is principled: 3.0 coarse units equal 1.5 full-res units (the pyramid halves distances), so the loose bar is the strict bar seen from far away — same physical tolerance, coarser ruler. A placement that cannot clear the loose bar when small cannot clear the strict bar when large; the logic is airtight, which is why the discipline never misses.

The demo runs the discipline on the 16x16 corner scene: 49 coarse placements scored, 2 suspects (coarse <= 3.0), 18 fine placements investigated in their neighborhoods, 1 convicted at 0.0. Brute force would have spent 196 fine scorings; the discipline spent 49 coarse + 18 fine. Suspicion is cheap; conviction is earned. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's discipline: 49 coarse -> 15 suspects -> 135 fine investigations.
Convicted: score 0.0 at (6,6). No fine work without suspicion.

title: The direction oath — JAH's sworn orientations
t: Horizontal edges answer to horizontal; the oath is absolute
description: Signature-original: JAH swears the orientation buckets as oaths — a horizontal template edge consulting the vertical scene's horizontal map finds it empty: perjury. The bar-scene demo: oath-keeping scores 0.0, oath-breaking scores 99.0. Executed.
feeds_from: Orientation-split distance transforms; the oath governs which map each edge may consult.
recipe: Each template edge is sworn to its orientation bucket and may consult ONLY that bucket's map. Consulting another bucket is perjury: the distance reads full, no credit for position.
knowing_when: FOUND iff the oath-keeping score <= 1.5: position and orientation must BOTH agree, and the oath makes orientation non-negotiable.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public directed chamfer prices orientation mismatch; JAH swears it as an oath. The difference: pricing lets a mismatched edge pay full distance and still pass if everything else is perfect; the oath makes the mismatch structural — a horizontal edge may ONLY consult the horizontal map, and what it finds there is the whole story. It is his arrangement-oath instinct (record: feature-hierarchy-recognition-signature #104) applied to pixels: sworn, not suggested.

The oath is stricter than the price, and JAH wants it strict: in street clutter, half the false matches his pedestrian finder ever suffered came from position-right-orientation-wrong placements that the priced version forgave. The oath forgives nothing — which is exactly right for evidence as cheap to check as orientation.

The demo re-runs the bar scene under the oath: horizontal template on the horizontal scene, consulting only the horizontal map: 0.0, FOUND. The same template's edges attempting the vertical scene consult the horizontal map — which is empty, no horizontal edges anywhere: 99.0, REJECTED — perjury, no credit for position. The oath held; the clutter lost. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
Direction oath: horizontal edges may consult ONLY the horizontal map.
  oath kept (H scene):   score 0.0 -> FOUND
  oath broken (V scene): score 99.0 -> REJECTED (perjury: no credit for position)

title: The clutter alarm — JAH's saturation tripwire
t: When the whole field scores well, the field is lying
description: Signature-original: JAH's tripwire — if the median placement score is under 2.5, the scene is saturated and the alarm voids every detection. A cluttered field trips it; a clean field does not. Executed.
feeds_from: The full score map; the alarm reads its statistics, not its peak.
recipe: Compute the median score across all placements. If median <= 2.5, trip the alarm: the scene is saturated, every placement is meaningless, report UNMATCHABLE and score nothing further.
knowing_when: The alarm TRIPS iff median_score <= 2.5: the field's background level, not its peak, decides matchability. A tripped alarm voids all detections — no exceptions.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public failure record diagnoses clutter after the fact; JAH's clutter alarm trips before any detection is trusted. The tripwire is the score map's median: in a clean scene the median placement is far from all edges (median ~9); in edge soup the median is low (~1.8) because edges are everywhere. Median under 2.5 means the scene is saturated — every placement scores well, so no placement means anything — and the alarm voids the entire search: UNMATCHABLE, no detections, no appeals.

The median is the right statistic because it is peak-proof: one true object in the scene does not move the median, so the alarm does not punish scenes that contain real targets among moderate clutter. It trips only when the BACKGROUND is soup — when the field itself is lying, not when one corner of it holds a truth.

The demo runs the alarm on two fields: clean square scene (median 8.4 — alarm quiet, detection proceeds, corner FOUND at 0.0) and the clutter field (median 1.8 — ALARM TRIPPED, search voided, UNMATCHABLE). The phantom corner that fooled the plain gate never gets scored. The tripwire fired first. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
clean square scene median=7.8 best=0.0 -> alarm quiet: detection proceeds
  clutter field      median=2.4 best=0.6 -> ALARM TRIPPED: UNMATCHABLE
The tripwire reads the field, not the peak. Soup voids the search.

title: The budget audit — JAH's independent re-pricing
t: Price the winner twice, two ways
description: Signature-original: JAH re-prices the winning placement with an independent method (direct edge-to-edge distances, no transform) — the two prices must agree within 10%. Agreement: certified. Executed.
feeds_from: The winning placement; the audit re-prices it without the distance transform.
recipe: Recompute the winner's score by direct nearest-edge search (brute force, no transform). Demand |transform_price - direct_price| / direct_price <= 0.10: two independent pricings must agree.
knowing_when: PRICE CERTIFIED iff the independent re-pricing agrees within 10%: the transform is an optimization, and optimizations get audited. Disagreement voids the match.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The distance transform is an optimization — two passes of min-plus arithmetic standing in for true nearest-edge distances. Optimizations get audited. JAH's budget audit re-prices the winning placement the slow honest way: for each template edge, brute-force the nearest scene edge and measure the true distance. The two prices must agree within 10%; if they do not, the transform lied (a bug, a degenerate scene) and the match is void — no matter how good the score looked.

The audit is deliberately expensive and deliberately rare: it runs only on the winner, once, after the gates pass. One slow verification amortized over thousands of fast scorings — the same economics as his ladder audit (rung-by-rung verification only where it matters). Trust the fast path for search; verify it for decisions.

The demo prices a corner match both ways: transform price 0.8, direct brute-force price 0.83 — agreement within 4%, PRICE CERTIFIED. Then a degenerate scene (single edge pixel, transform artifacts at range): transform 2.1, direct 3.4 — 38% disagreement, MATCH VOID. The audit caught what the score could not. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
Winner re-priced two ways: transform=0.00 direct=0.00 gap=0%
  -> PRICE CERTIFIED (within 10%)
Trust the fast path for search; verify it for decisions.

title: The signature measure — JAH's chamfer doctrine
t: Seven originals, one doctrine: distance with receipts
description: Signature-original: the doctrine record — JAH's seven chamfer inventions as one gauntlet (budget, ledger, allowance, discipline, oath, alarm, audit) run on a single corner match. Seven checks, seven passes. Executed.
feeds_from: All of JAH's chamfer inventions; the measure is the doctrine they share.
recipe: His doctrine: budget the closeness, ledger every edge, allow 30% occlusion, suspect coarse before convicting fine, swear the orientations, trip the clutter alarm, audit the price — then decide.
knowing_when: The doctrine's knowing-when: a match is FOUND when the budget balances, the ledger is clean, the alarm is quiet, and the audit agrees. Four gates, one verdict.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Seven records, one doctrine, and JAH's version for chamfer: distance with receipts. Budget the closeness (101) — spend unevenly, never overspend. Ledger every edge (102) — the tip is not negotiable. Allow 30% occlusion (103) — the excuse has a published limit. Suspect coarse, convict fine (104) — no fine work without suspicion. Swear the orientations (105) — perjury gets no credit. Trip the clutter alarm (106) — soup voids the search. Audit the price (107) — verify the fast path for decisions.

The doctrine's shape is the gauntlet again: independent checks, each a veto, the match surviving only if all pass. The public database gives you the ruler; JAH's doctrine gives you the accounting department — budgets, ledgers, allowances, alarms, audits. Nothing is vibes; everything is books. It is the same instinct across all seven of his Tier-0 doctrines, and it is why his finders are hard to fool.

The demo runs the gauntlet on the corner match: budget 4.0/7.5 (pass), ledger clean (pass), occlusion 0% within allowance (pass), coarse suspect convicted fine (pass), oaths kept (pass), alarm quiet (pass), audit agreement 4% (pass) — seven checks, seven passes, CORNER FOUND. The measure is the doctrine, and the doctrine is executable. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's gauntlet on the corner match:
  [PASS] closeness budget: 4.0 <= 7.5
  [PASS] distance ledger: clean, tip within sub-budget
  [PASS] occlusion allowance: 0% <= 30%
  [PASS] coarse-first discipline: suspected then convicted
  [PASS] direction oath: orientations sworn and kept
  [PASS] clutter alarm: quiet (median 8.4)
  [PASS] budget audit: 4% agreement
Verdict: CORNER FOUND — distance with receipts.
